title: Slow-tier landing validation -- PREDICTION CONFIRMED
result: PASS. All 3 segments reached target inside the 0.15 m tolerance under test, with ZERO turn commands, zero errors, and no reverse-recovery containment.
key_findings: Prediction confirmed: the error budget (feed staleness ~10 cm + stop latency 2-5 cm at slow tier) predicted ~0.15 m and every run landed inside it.

EVERY segment UNDERSHOT (ratios 0.880-0.978). Gate 4 at 0.08 m overshot at 2.19x and required a U-turn recovery. Same control law, same profile -- only the tolerance changed. At 0.08 the mower cannot confirm arrival before passing the point; at 0.15 it stops on the first approach.

0.08 m is marginal rather than impossible: 2 of 3 runs would have met it (0.0317 and 0.0882 just outside). Intermittent success is worse than reliable failure because it produces sporadic recovery maneuvers -- which is exactly what the beta20/beta21 Gate 4 passes did.
Zero turn commands across all three segments, so this isolates LINEAR landing accuracy as intended.

method.heading: Established by motion, not telemetry: one 0.372 m forward pulse gave map heading 277.433 deg; each subsequent segment re-derived heading from the previous segment displacement.
method.why: toward is course-over-ground and reads frozen while stationary -- it was identical (172.1591) before and after an overnight gap.
method.measurement: error = |settled_position - target| from the position feed after a 4 s settle; stationary noise under Fix is sub-cm.

gate: armed immediately before, disarmed immediately after; verified both times
